quote: These findings indicate that there exists a “mental number line” for children in the process of numerical comparison. Moyer and Landauer (1967) were the first to measure the RT in a selection paradigm by pressing the associated button. They found that participants made more mistakes and required more time when the two numbers to be compared were close (e.g., 7 vs. 9) than farther apart (e.g., 2 vs. 9).
